entries.test: Whether Marcus's May 2023 Senate testimony, a 2023 Substack essay and his 2024 book Taming Silicon Valley advocate preflight, FDA-style testing for large-scale AI models.
entries.note: The sentence says what he argued in the past. The drafter turned it into a present 'should' claim, which he implies but does not state here.

entries.test: Whether any US federal preflight-testing requirement for AI was adopted between 2023 and January 2025, and whether the Trump administration reversed AI policy (for example, by revoking Biden's AI executive order).
entries.note: Context makes it fair to limit 'nothing happened' to preflight testing and AI regulation.

entries.test: Whether, in early 2026, the White House and Congress were broadly hostile to AI regulation, for example by pursuing federal preemption or moratoria on state AI laws.
entries.note: 'Seemed hopeless' is his impression. The hostility claim underneath it can be tested.

entries.test: Whether the White House began any pre-deployment government testing of frontier models in response to the Anthropic Mythos episode in spring 2026.
entries.note: The 'to some degree' hedge is kept. 'Consider' is dropped, but the firmer 'implement' part is still there.

entries.test: Whether Hassabis published an essay around July 2026 backing pre-release review of frontier models by a standards body.
entries.note: The quoted passage suggests voluntary sharing of models up to 30 days before release.
His statement that the US government was considering taking stakes in AI companies is a separate fact. Here it only supports the 'must'.
'Excellent' and 'a better place' judge worth; neither gives a measurable outcome. The proposition leaves out 'excellent'.
